summary: Atsushi Kanazawa specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1972–1980), lectured at the Meteorological College (attested 1986–1989), and held posts at Komazawa University from around 1993 to 2003.
Atsushi Kiyozawa is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Delhi. In 1989, he held an attested lecturer position at Kindai University.

Indologist and philosopher Atsushi Uno studied at Kyoto University, Banaras Hindu University, and under Raghunath Giri, Vamacharana Bhattacharya, and T. R. V. Murti. He held professorships at Tokai, Hiroshima (1974–1986), and Kindai (~1986–1993) universities.

Atsuuji Ashikaga worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Doshisha and Kyoto universities under Ryosaburo Sakaki, he held faculty posts at Kyoto University (1930–1962) and served as president of the Society for Near Eastern Studies in Japan.
Atsuyoshi Keika works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a lecturer (attested 1990) and later as a professor (attested 2014) at Otani University.

August Boeckh worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. Educated at Halle-Wittenberg under F. A. Wolf and F. Schleiermacher, he held professorships at Heidelberg University (1807–1811) and the University of Berlin (1811–1861).

August Conrady specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Würzburg and Leipzig, later holding academic posts at the University of Leipzig from 1891 to 1922 and at Peking University (1903–1904).

August Ferdinand Naeke specialized in linguistics, history, and archaeology. After studying at the University of Leipzig (~1806–1810), he held posts at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1813–1818) and the University of Bonn (~1818–1838).

August Fick worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen (1852–1856), where he became an extraordinary professor in 1876, later serving as an ordinary professor at the University of Breslau (1887–1891).

August Fischer specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1885–1889) and served as a professor at the University of Leipzig from around 1900 to 1930.

August Friedrich Pott was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Göttingen and under Franz Bopp in Berlin, briefly lecturing at Berlin (1830) before serving as a professor of general linguistics at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1833.

August Hermann Francke specialized in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at the Lehrerseminar Niesky, Moravian College, and Humboldt University of Berlin, where he served as Privatdozent (1922) and extraordinary professor (1925).

Linguist and Indologist August Hjalmar Edgren studied at Uppsala, Cornell, and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He taught at Yale (1874–1880), Lund (1880–1884), Nebraska-Lincoln (~1885–1891), and served as rector of the University of Gothenburg (1891–1893).

August Johan Bernet Kempers worked in archaeology, history, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (~1926–1933) and directed the Archaeological Service of the Netherlands East Indies (~1936–1956), later holding a post at the University of Amsterdam (1969–1984).

Linguist and Indologist August Leskien studied at Leipzig, Kiel, and Jena under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. He served as professor at the University of Jena (1868) and the University of Leipzig (1870–1915).

August Schleicher worked in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Leipzig, Tübingen, and Bonn under Heinrich Ewald, Christian Lassen, and others, he held professorships at Charles University (1850–1857) and the University of Jena from 1857.
August Sundin is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar attested in 2026 as a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University.

August Tholuck worked in religious studies and linguistics. After studying at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1817–1820), he held posts there (~1820–1826) and at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1826–1877).

Indologist and linguist August Wilhelm von Schlegel studied at Göttingen and under Antoine-Léonard Chézy and Alexander Hamilton. He served as professor at the University of Jena (1795, 1798) and held the first Indology chair at the University of Bonn (1818).

Auguste Barth worked in Indology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Strasbourg (~1852–1856), he taught at Collège Poincaré Saverne (~1856–1860) and was a member of the Institut de France (~1893–1916).
